episodes.169331: Some upper level energy, a surface front, and diurnal heating contributed to scattered thunderstorms in the late afternoon and evening, a few of which reached severe limits.
episodes.169342: A trough over the Pacific Northwest sent a shortwave up and over an upper level ridge parked over central Montana.  This would set off a round of severe thunderstorms during the afternoon hours.
episodes.169353: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain to southwestern Chester County during the afternoon and early evening of July 2.  Rainfall totals were as high as 3.5 to 4.5 inches.
episodes.169385: A Pacific trough sat to the west and an upper level ridge was to the east near the Montana and North Dakota border, placing northeast Montana under southwesterly flow aloft.  A shortwave riding up this upper level flow moved through and sent a line of thunderstorms through the area during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.169392: A cold front dropped down from the north, causing showers and thunderstorms to develop. The storm motion was nearly parallel to the boundary, causing some storms to train over the same area. This led to instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.169396: A cold front dropped down from the north, causing showers and thunderstorms to develop. The storm motion was nearly parallel to the boundary, causing some storms to train over the same area. This led to instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.169408: Scattered thunderstorms developed across northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon and evening of the 3rd. The air mass across the area had become moderately unstable when the storms developed, but the wind shear was weak, which resulted in brief, intense thunderstorms. The strongest thunderstorm produced damaging wind.
episodes.169500: A shortwave trough moving eastward from the eastern Great Lakes, triggered strong thunderstorms in New York state, which moved into southern New England overnight.  The atmosphere was very unstable and surface dewpoints were near 70 degrees. The result was strong to locally severe thunderstorms before daybreak in southeast MA.  Sunshine boosted temperatures in the afternoon, then a cold front swept through in the evening hours, triggering a second round of strong to severe thunderstorms, mainly in western and central MA.
episodes.169527: A line of severe thunderstorms developed over Fall River and Custer Counties, producing wind gusts to 70 mph as it moved east across much of southwestern South Dakota.
episodes.169528: Very hot temperatures on the afternoon of the third and an approaching weak mid-level circulation allowed for isolated to scattered thunderstorms to develop off the caprock. Relatively dry sub-cloud layers allowed for strong downburst winds to develop which produced a couple of severe wind gusts near Hackberry (Cottle County) and near Silverton (Briscoe County).
episodes.169529: A supercell thunderstorm tracked southeast across northern and eastern portions of Harding County before weakening. The storm produced large hail and wind gusts to 70 mph.
episodes.170029: Low pressure along the west coast spread deeper moisture increasing the chances for showers and thunderstorms across the region through Independence Day. These storms brought strong, gusty winds, severe hail, moderate to heavy rainfall, and lightning, causing notable damage to property, specifically crops.
episodes.170195: A deep trough of low pressure across western Washington and Oregon generated enough lift, moisture and wind shear to initiate several severe thunderstorms across western Montana.
episodes.170446: An unstable southwest flow aloft, combined with a strong jet stream aloft and a moist low-level easterly flow, resulted in numerous severe thunderstorms across the Billings Forecast Area. These thunderstorms contained large hail and very heavy rain.
episodes.170600: A few severe thunderstorms produced several instances of wind damage ahead of a cold front during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.170601: A few severe thunderstorms produced several instances of wind damage ahead of a cold front during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.170808: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over western Fall River County, producing wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.170809: A thunderstorm briefly became severe in the Summerset area, producing hail around quarter size.
episodes.170812: A severe thunderstorm developed over eastern Pennington County and tracked north-northeast into southeastern Meade County before weakening. The storm produced very large hail around baseball size over portions of eastern Pennington County.
episodes.170814: A severe thunderstorm developed southwest of Philip and tracked east-northeast across southern Haakon County. The storm produced large hail and strong wind gusts across the area.
episodes.170816: A thunderstorm briefly became severe in the Sturgis area, producing hail around quarter size.
episodes.170837: A few thunderstorms produced several instances of gale force winds ahead of a cold front during the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.170887: A pair of thunderstorms passed over Rock Springs during the afternoon and evening. High winds occurred at the Sweetwater County Airport to the east of Rock Springs. No damage was reported.
episodes.171030: A weakening and slow moving complex of storms moved into southeast Arkansas on the morning of July 3rd. The slow movement combined with heavy rainfall rates resulted in flash flooding in Ashley County.
episodes.171092: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the region producing isolated areas of wind damage and hail across the area. One storm impacted portions of Monmouth County and another isolated storm produced a 50 kt wind gust in Cumberland County.
episodes.171095: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the region producing isolated areas of wind damage and hail across the area. Training cells produced a couple instances of tree damage in southern Chester County in addition to heavy rainfall resulting in some localized flooding.
episodes.171326: Thunderstorms resulted in a lightning fatality at Masonboro Island.
episodes.171399: Severe thunderstorms initiated near a surface low and weak frontal zone in northeast Montana. The storms then moved into western North Dakota, spreading south along the front, while the whole complex move towards the southeast. Strong wind gusts were the main threats with these storms, with the strongest reported wind gust of 82 mph occurring in Slope County. One-inch diameter hail occurred in Mountrail and McLean counties.
episodes.171615: Southwesterly flow prevailed with the high pressure ridge extending over the area from the Bermuda high. This flow regime kept the Atlantic sea breeze pinned to the coastline with the sea breeze merger happening east of I-95. Warm mid level temperatures and high moisture content with PWATs over 2 inches led to efficient rainfall rates in storms and locally heavy rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches. A lack of shear, typical for this time of year, and poor lapse rates limited wind gusts associated with wet downbursts to stay around 40 mph or less. Frequent lightning also accompanied the strongest storms.
episodes.171960: On July 3rd, a warm front passed through the northwestern region of Kansas which allowed thunderstorms to develop. These thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts up to an estimated 95 mph as well as hail up to peas in size. Not only did the thunderstorms knock out power due to the damaging winds in Sherman county, but lightning from a thunderstorm was reported to have struck a substation in Decatur County, knocking out power for a good portion of the county.
episodes.171964: Persistent heavy rainfall brought flash flooding to the southern part of the state.
episodes.172023: A weak upper low pressure system teamed with moisture from a remnant tropical low to bring widely scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms to the region in the first few days of July. Minor wind damage associated with these storms was reported in a few isolated locations.
episodes.172062: An isolated supercell developed during the afternoon of July 3rd, producing hail up to 1 inch across portions of the southern Red River Valley and west-central Minnesota. In addition to 1-inch hail, a well-defined wall cloud was identified.
episodes.172105: An active tropical wave moved across the area. This wave brought periods of heavy rainfall, along with strong gusty winds, resulting in multiple flood reports.
episodes.172159: A west to east oriented shear axis aloft extended along the Middle Red River Valley of North Texas into Southeast Oklahoma to along the Arkansas/Louisiana border during the morning hours of July 3rd, which enhanced large scale forcing for the development of a concentrated area of showers and thunderstorms over portions of Southern Arkansas. A very moist environment was in place across this area as well, which enhanced rain rates as these showers and thunderstorms remained nearly stationary over much of Union County Arkansas through much of the morning hours after daybreak. Widespread rainfall amounts of 3-6 inches fell across Union County, with isolated higher amounts of 7-9+ inches measured across Northern and Central portions of the county. This resulted in widespread flash flooding across much of Union County, flooding and washing away multiple roads, with high water entering multiple buildings in El Dorado. These showers and thunderstorms diminished during the afternoon hours on the 3rd.
episodes.172185: Thunderstorms moved northward out of north Texas during the afternoon of the 3rd with a few reports of severe wind gusts reported across southern Oklahoma.
episodes.172194: An area of low pressure slowly crossing the region brought severe storms to central South Dakota during the early morning hours of July 3rd. Winds exceeding 65 mph caused tree damage around the Pierre area. A peak wind gust of 69 mph was reported at the Pierre Municipal Airport.
episodes.172195: Thunderstorms developed over central South Dakota along a warm front. An isolated severe storm produced wind damage to a mature tree one-mile south-southwest of Ree Heights.
episodes.172199: Scattered thunderstorms developed across parts of southern Colorado late in the day and into the evening. The strongest storms occurred across Pueblo County, where damaging winds up to 65 mph and heavy rainfall with localized flash flooding occurred.
episodes.172473: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.172566: A severe weather outbreak main affected the Upper Snake River Plain with rrports of greater than 50 knot winds, large hail and lightning strikes.
episodes.172607: A surface trough and southward advancing cold front led to showers and storms tracking northwest to southeast, largely across the southern Piedmont, Sandhills, and Coastal Plain. While most of the storms were not severe, one storm did produce wind gusts to 60 miles per hour and nickel size hail in Montgomery County.
episodes.172628: A mid-level trough across the Great Lakes helped push a weak cold front into the central North Carolina Piedmont during the evening and overnight hours. Ahead of the front, storms over the Ohio Valley and West Virginia produced additional surface boundaries across the northern Piedmont. The approach of the front led to development of scattered to numerous showers and storms across the northwest Piedmont in the late-evening hours, tapering off around midnight. The strongest storms produced downed trees and flash flooding in Forsyth County.
episodes.172662: A lone thunderstorm developed along a weak low-level convergence zone which featured around 1500-2000 J/kg MLCAPE and deep-layer shear around 40 knots. An isolated supercell developed and produced considerable hail, and occasional large hail.
episodes.172669: A weak synoptic-scale wave progressed through the area atop a flat upper-level ridge, initiating several clusters of thunderstorms during the afternoon and early evening.  Storms developed near a weak convergence zone, in an environment of 1000-2000 J/kg MLCAPE and marginally strong deep-layer shear of 30 knots.  Mainly multi-cell clusters resulted in marginally severe damaging wind gusts due to sub-cloud dryness and marginally large hail.
episodes.172765: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina foothills during the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced hail in Burke County.
episodes.172836: An upper low in the eastern Pacific guided a moisture plume over the region, resulting in numerous rain showers developing across the region. Increasing instability from southerly flow aloft also resulted in thunderstorms developing, with a few storms producing hail stones over an inch in diameter, strong winds, and brief heavy downpours.
episodes.172838: A slow moving low moved through the region over July 3 through July 5. It carried ample moisture and instability to produce several rounds of thunderstorms and heavy rains. The thunderstorms produced hail, high winds, and lightning. The heavy rains created flash flooding.
episodes.173037: Aided by a weak disturbance moving off the Georgia coast, showers and thunderstorms developed within an abnormally moist tropical airmass along converging outflow boundaries. These pulse convective storms produced isolated reports of trees and powerlines down in west-central Georgia.
episodes.173064: Typical afternoon summertime showers and thunderstorms developed within a modestly unstable and abnormally moist tropical airmass during the afternoon and evening of July 3rd. These storms produced widespread reports of trees and powerlines down across portions of north and central Georgia.
